title: Implement a New 'Testimonials' Feature (Data Layer and API Endpoint)
description: This is a multi-session task to add a new 'testimonials' feature to the PortfolioPals web application. In the first session, the agent will implement the data layer, defining the data structure and database insertion logic. In the second session, the agent must build upon the first session's work to create a public API endpoint that allows visitors to submit new testimonials. This task tests the agent's ability to retain context, understand a simple C web application architecture, and perform incremental development.

project_spec.name: PortfolioPals
project_spec.description:
PortfolioPals is a light-weight social web-portfolio platform written in C that lets creatives publish personal portfolios while following, liking and commenting on each other’s work. Although the functional surface is intentionally small to keep the project beginner-friendly, it still demonstrates a full MVC stack: models for users, projects and interactions; views rendered into responsive HTML/CSS; and controllers that expose both classic web routes and JSON API endpoints. The social layer—followers, activity feed and OAuth log-ins—sets this project apart from a typical portfolio site, making collaboration and feedback the core experience.

The codebase is structured around the MVC pattern using a minimal C HTTP server library. Controllers handle routing, dispatch authentication middleware and delegate persistence to repositories backed by an embedded SQLite database accessed through a tiny ORM wrapper. The admin panel, file-upload for project images, input validation, consistent error handling and social-login providers (Google & GitHub) are integrated to illustrate common real-world concerns while remaining approachable for newcomers to C web development.
dependencies: cJSON (JSON parsing and serialization for REST API responses)
sqlc (small C ORM-style wrapper used for Database_ORM pattern)
libjwt / jws (JWT creation & validation for session and API tokens)
Mustach or ClearSilver (logic-less HTML template rendering for Views)
OAuth2-c (minimal OAuth2 client for Google/GitHub social login)
cmocka (unit-testing, helps verify data-validation and repository logic)
